findings.title: SQL Injection via Unsanitized User Input in Login and Product Search
findings.description: The login endpoint at routes/login.ts:34 directly interpolates req.body.email into a raw SQL query string. Similarly, routes/search.ts:25 interpolates req.query.q into a raw SQL query. Neither endpoint sanitizes or parameterizes the input. An unauthenticated attacker can extract the entire database contents including password hashes and payment card numbers.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace raw SQL string interpolation with parameterized queries. At routes/login.ts:34, use models.sequelize.query('SELECT * FROM Users WHERE email = ? AND password = ? AND deletedAt IS NULL', { replacements: [req.body.email, security.hash(req.body.password)], model: UserModel, plain: true }).

findings.title: denyAll() Bypass via JWT Algorithm None Attack on express-jwt 0.1.3
findings.description: The denyAll() middleware at lib/insecurity.ts:55 uses expressJwt({ secret: '' + Math.random() }). This relies on express-jwt version 0.1.3 which has a known vulnerability allowing algorithm substitution attacks (alg:none). If an attacker sends a JWT with "alg": "none" and removes the signature, express-jwt 0.1.3 may accept it, bypassing both isAuthorized() and denyAll() protection.
findings.suggested_fix: Upgrade express-jwt to version e6.0.0 which rejects alg:none by default. At lib/insecurity.ts:55, explicitly specify allowed algorithms: expressJwt({ secret: ..., algorithms: ['RS256'] }).

findings.title: Server-Side Template Injection / RCE via eval() on Stored Username
findings.description: The getUserProfile() function at routes/userProfile.ts:57 evaluates the user's stored username using eval(code) when the username matches the pattern #{(...)}. A user can set their username to #{require('child_process').execSync('id').toString()} via POST /profile. When the profile page is subsequently rendered, the stored username is eval'd, achieving RCE.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the eval() call entirely at routes/userProfile.ts:57. Replace the dynamic template compilation with a safe templating approach that doesn't evaluate arbitrary code.

findings.title: XML External Entity (XXE) Injection via Unauthenticated File Upload
findings.description: The XML file upload handler at routes/fileUpload.ts:83 parses uploaded XML with libxml.parseXml(data, { noblanks: true, noent: true, nocdata: true }). The noent: true option enables XML entity expansion, which allows XXE attacks. The endpoint is completely unauthenticated (no auth middleware in server.ts:309).
findings.suggested_fix: Disable external entity expansion by removing noent: true from the XML parsing options at routes/fileUpload.ts:84. Change to: libxml.parseXml(data, { noblanks: true, noent: false, nocdata: true }).

findings.title: Remote Code Execution via Sandbox Escape in B2B Order Endpoint
findings.description: The B2B order endpoint at routes/b2bOrder.ts:23 evaluates user-supplied orderLinesData from the request body using safeEval (from the notevil package v1.3.3) within a Node.js VM context. The notevil package has known sandbox escape vulnerabilities that allow arbitrary code execution.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the eval-based processing entirely. Replace safeEval(orderLinesData) with a safe JSON parser: JSON.parse(orderLinesData) at routes/b2bOrder.ts:23.

findings.title: Password Change Without Current Password Verification and Credentials in URL/Logs
findings.description: The password change endpoint at routes/changePassword.ts:13 uses HTTP GET method, accepting passwords as URL query parameters. At line 39, the current password verification is conditional: if (currentPassword && security.hash(currentPassword) !== loggedInUser.data.password) - when currentPassword is empty/undefined, the check is skipped entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: At routes/changePassword.ts:39, make current password always required: change if (currentPassword && ...) to if (!currentPassword || security.hash(currentPassword) !== loggedInUser.data.password). Change the endpoint from GET to POST.

findings.title: Stored XSS via bypassSecurityTrustHtml in Admin Panel and About Page
findings.description: The application uses bypassSecurityTrustHtml() in the Angular frontend to render user-controlled content without sanitization. At frontend/src/app/administration/administration.component.ts:73, user emails are rendered via bypassSecurityTrustHtml. At about.component.ts:119, feedback comments are rendered unsafely in the public about page.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove bypassSecurityTrustHtml() calls at administration.component.ts:73 and :91 and about.component.ts:119. Use Angular's built-in sanitization by binding to [textContent] instead of [innerHTML].

findings.title: NoSQL Injection via $where Clause in Order Tracking Endpoint
findings.description: The track-order endpoint at routes/trackOrder.ts:18 interpolates the user-supplied path parameter id directly into a MongoDB $where clause: db.ordersCollection.find({ $where: `this.orderId === '${id}'` }). When reflectedXssChallenge is enabled, the id is only truncated to 60 characters, which is sufficient for NoSQL injection.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the $where JavaScript injection with a safe MongoDB query. At routes/trackOrder.ts:18, change to: db.ordersCollection.find({ orderId: id }).

findings.title: Order PDFs Containing Customer PII Exposed via Public FTP Directory
findings.description: Order confirmation PDFs are written to the /ftp directory at routes/order.ts:45. The /ftp directory has public directory listing enabled without authentication at server.ts:269. The PDFs contain customer email, order items, prices, and delivery addresses.
findings.suggested_fix: Move order PDFs to a non-publicly-served directory. Add authentication middleware to the /ftp route: app.use('/ftp', security.isAuthorized(), ...).

findings.title: Hardcoded Test Credentials Exposed in Client-Side JavaScript
findings.description: Test credentials are hardcoded in the client-side login component at frontend/src/app/login/login.component.ts:63-64: public testingUsername = 'testing@juice-sh.op' and public testingPassword = 'IamUsedForTesting'. These are compiled into the JavaScript bundle served to all visitors.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove hardcoded credentials from the frontend code at login.component.ts:63-64. If testing credentials are needed, use environment-specific configuration that is not compiled into production builds.

findings.title: Hardcoded Ethereum Wallet Mnemonic in Source Code
findings.description: An Ethereum wallet mnemonic phrase is hardcoded at routes/checkKeys.ts:10. From this mnemonic, the HD wallet private key, public key, and address are derived (lines 11-14). Anyone with access to the source code can derive the private key and potentially access funds.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the wallet mnemonic to an environment variable or secrets manager. At routes/checkKeys.ts:10, replace with: const mnemonic = process.env.ETH_WALLET_MNEMONIC.

findings.title: [Requirement: Authorization Best Practices] Missing and broken authorization controls allowing IDOR, privilege escalation, and unauthorized data modification
findings.description: The basket access endpoint at routes/basket.ts:17 retrieves a basket by :id without verifying ownership. The password change at routes/changePassword.ts:39 skips verification when field is empty. The Product PUT endpoint at server.ts:369 has its authorization commented out entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: At routes/basket.ts:18, add ownership check: BasketModel.findOne({ where: { id, UserId: req.body.UserId } }). At server.ts:369, uncomment and strengthen authorization to require admin role for product modification.

findings.title: [Requirement: Secret Protection Best Practices] Cryptographic secrets hardcoded in source code without rotation or secure storage
findings.description: The RSA private key used for JWT signing is hardcoded in plain text at lib/insecurity.ts:24. This key is used to sign all JWT tokens (insecurity.ts:56 authorize function). Additionally, an HMAC secret pa4qacea4VK9t9nGv7yZtwmj is hardcoded at lib/insecurity.ts:44.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the RSA private key and HMAC secret to environment variables or a secrets management service. At lib/insecurity.ts:24, replace with: const privateKey = process.env.JWT_PRIVATE_KEY || fs.readFileSync(process.env.JWT_KEY_PATH).

findings.title: [Requirement: Authentication Best Practices] Hardcoded credentials, forgeable JWT tokens, and bypassable authentication controls
findings.description: Multiple critical authentication failures: (1) JWT private key hardcoded enabling token forging. (2) Hardcoded passwords in login challenge verification (routes/login.ts:60-66). (3) Password change skips verification when field is empty. (4) Rate limiting is keyed on spoofable X-Forwarded-For header.
findings.suggested_fix: Move JWT private key to environment variable. Remove all hardcoded credentials from login.ts challenge verification. At changePassword.ts:39, always require current password. Use a reliable client identifier for rate limiting.

findings.title: [Requirement: Trusted Cryptography Best Practices] MD5 used for password hashing and weak 1024-bit RSA key for JWT signing
findings.description: The application uses MD5 (unsalted) for password hashing at lib/insecurity.ts:43: crypto.createHash('md5').update(data).digest('hex'). This hash function is applied to all user passwords via the User model setter at models/user.ts:68. MD5 is cryptographically broken. Additionally, the JWT signing uses a 1024-bit RSA key which is below the recommended 2048-bit minimum.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace MD5 with bcrypt or argon2 for password hashing. At lib/insecurity.ts:43, change to: export const hash = (data: string) => bcrypt.hashSync(data, 12). Generate a new RSA key pair of at least 2048 bits.

findings.title: [Requirement: Information Protection Best Practices] Sensitive data transmitted without encryption and stored without protection
findings.description: Cookies are set without the Secure flag at lib/insecurity.ts:195: res.cookie('token', token) - no secure: true option. This allows JWT tokens to be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP. Payment card numbers are stored as plain integers (DataTypes.INTEGER) in the database at models/card.ts:39-45 without encryption at rest.
findings.suggested_fix: At lib/insecurity.ts where cookies are set, add security flags: res.cookie('token', token, { secure: true, httpOnly: true, sameSite: 'strict' }). Encrypt card numbers at rest using application-level encryption (e.g., AES-256-GCM).

findings.title: [Requirement: Secure by Default Best Practices] Insecure defaults including unrestricted CORS, disabled authorization, and public admin endpoints
findings.description: The authorization for PUT /api/Products/:id is commented out at server.ts:369. The CORS configuration at server.ts:182 uses wildcard (app.options('*', cors()); app.use(cors())), allowing cross-origin requests from any domain. The admin configuration endpoint at server.ts:606 requires no authentication.
findings.suggested_fix: At server.ts:369, uncomment the authorization. At server.ts:182, configure CORS with explicit origins. At server.ts:606, add admin authentication.

findings.title: [Requirement: Audit Logging Best Practices] No security event logging for authentication, authorization, or data modification events
findings.description: The application has no security event logging beyond basic HTTP access logging via Morgan at server.ts:338. The login handler at routes/login.ts:19-75 does not log failed authentication attempts. The password change handler does not log password changes. No structured audit logging exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Add structured security event logging. At routes/login.ts, log after each login attempt: logger.info({ event: 'login_attempt', email, success: !!user.data?.id, ip: req.ip, timestamp: new Date() }).

findings.title: [Requirement: Privileged Access Best Practices] Administrative endpoints unprotected and lacking audit logging of privileged actions
findings.description: The admin configuration endpoint at server.ts:606 (GET /rest/admin/application-configuration) has no authentication middleware. There is no audit logging for privileged actions. The admin panel allows user deletion, feedback removal, and delivery status toggling without any audit trail.
findings.suggested_fix: At server.ts:606, add admin authentication: app.get('/rest/admin/application-configuration', security.isAuthorized(), isAdmin(), ...). Add audit logging middleware for all state-changing administrative operations.

findings.title: [Requirement: Log Protection Best Practices] Log Files Served Publicly Without Authentication
findings.description: The application's log files are served publicly without authentication at server.ts:280-282. The Morgan 'combined' format access logs at server.ts:338 record full request URLs including query parameters. Since the password change endpoint uses GET with passwords in query strings, the access logs contain plaintext passwords.
findings.suggested_fix: At server.ts:280, add authentication to the logs endpoint: app.use('/support/logs', security.isAuthorized(), isAdmin(), ...). Redact sensitive query parameters from the Morgan format before writing to logs.
